newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: De Boer, Unigro detail merger structure.
newsitem.headline: De Boer, Unigro detail merger structure.

text.p: The planned merger between Dutch supermarket chains De Boer Winkelbedrijven and Unigro will result in a combine with some 10.6 million shares outstanding, the two companies said.
"De Boer currently has some 4.6 million shares outstanding and this will be supplemented by another six million," Unigro finance director Wouter Kranenberg told a news conference.

Under the deal clinched between the two companies, shares in unlisted Unigro will go to De Boer Winkelbedrijven in return for (non-voting) depositary receipts of shares in the new combine, De Boer Unigro.

Unigro's present holding company will initially gain a stake of 57 percent in the new combine, in line with the assets Unigro will bring to the alliance, the new company's future chairman Robert ter Haar said.

"But because this merger is intended on the basis of equality, the Unigro holding company will have to reduce its stake to 49.9 percent within six months," he said. No decision had as yet been taken on how it would do this, Ter Haar added.
Part of the shares acquired by the Unigro holding would be transferred to an independent foundation, but the precise breakdown of shareholdings had not yet been decided, he said.
"The free flow of shares (in the new company) will be the same as, or bigger than, is currently the case," Ter Haar said.
Elaborating, Kranenberg said that in absolute terms the number of freely traded depositary receipts of share would rise.
Some 75 percent of De Boer's 4.6 million outstanding shares is currently freely tradeable. Existing De Boer shares will be be converted to shares in the new combine.

The price for Unigro's assets further includes one million warrants on De Boer Unigro shares. These can be swapped for shares in the new combine at a strike price of 105 guilders a share within five years.
However the exercise of the warrants cannot be allowed to lead to Unigro's holding company lifting its stake in the combine to more than 49.9 percent, Kranenberg said.
"In that case the holding would simply have to sell the shares on," he told journalists.
All Unigro shares are now held by Albada Jelgersma Holding BV, an investment vehicle fully-owned by Unigro's former chief executive Eric Albada Jelgersma.
